newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close in sharp loss, Eurotunnel up.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close in sharp loss, Eurotunnel up.

text.p: All CAC-40 stocks closed with losses on Wednesday with only Eurotunnel showing a gain and Cie Generale des Eaux unchanged. The index stood at a support level of 2,308 level after pulling back from year highs.
Traders said the market needed to take profits before resuming its advance with the goal of regaining the historic high of 2,360.98 points set in 1994.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 40.46 points or 1.72 percent at 2,308.65, while the CAC-40 futures contract fell to 2,310 from 2,352 on Tuesday's close.
Volume was solid 6.5 billion francs.
* Support seen at 2,308, 2,280, and 2,240 points on the CAC index, with resistance seen at 2,355, 2,368 and 2,375.
* A trader at a French bank said some operators were caught wrong-footed by the 80-point drop on Wall Street and the 2,308 support could be breached on Thursday.
* A further correction could be healthy for the market after a straight line run up since the end of August.
* Lagardere fell seven percent to 145 francs, hit hard by suspension of the Thomson privatisation and ensuing uncertainty. Some 275 million francs worth of stock traded.
* Alcatel Alsthom fell 3.18 percent to 460 francs on the fallout from the government's retreat on the controversial Thomson sale.
"The government was under so much pressure. It doesn't come as a surprise," said a broker. "It probably puts (Prime Minister) Juppe under more pressure."
* Thomson-CSF fell 3.37 percent to 160.50 francs.

* Rhone-Poulenc eased 3.41 percent to 167 francs on market talk of a merger with Schering, which denied the rumour. Some 227 million francs of Rhone stock traded. Rhone has been a persistent target of merger speculation.
* Trading was active in Usinor, Bic and AGF, considered candidates to take UAP's place on the CAC if the UAP-Axa merger goes through.

Steelmaker Usinor rose 2.48 percent to 82.80, Bic fell 0.25 percent to 810, after earlier adding two percent, and AGF ended down 3.81 percent at 166.6 as operators switched out of the insurer into the steel firm.
* Cie Bancaire also busy, ending down 0.95 percent at 627. It limited losses as extra property provisions pleased the market. Some 218 million francs of shares traded.
* Carrefour weakened three percent to 3,250.
It has had a strong run up as a blue chip favoured by international investors.
* Eurotunnel, a stock favoured by market professionals for speculative trading, closed up 3.6 percent at 7.20 francs. A reduced Eurostar passenger service restarted today.
* Some operators expect the Bank of France may cut interest rates as early as Thursday at its money market tender.

* Galeries Lafayette shed 3.2 percent to 1,752 francs, BHV fell 2.64 percent to 480, and Pinault- Printemps-Redoute eased 0.73 percent to 2,050, on fears yesterday's Paris bomb attack could scare shoppers away.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
